text.p: - Turnout at Slovenia's second general election on Sunday was 73.5 percent, the country's electoral commission said on Tuesday.
- Succcessor states of former Yugoslavia presented their proposals about the division of the former federation's assets to international negotiator Sir Arthur Watts on Tuesday.
- Reconstruction of the Karavanke border tunnel between Austria and Slovenia started on Tuesday. Work is expected to be finished in one month.
- Slovenian parties that entered the parliament after the Sunday's election started negotiations on forming a coalition on Tuesday.
- The new parliament should convene for the first time before the end of November, according to the country's constitution.
- Slovenia will probably decide about the purchase of new fighter aircraft next year. Currently the Netherlands is promoting its F-16 aircrafts on Slovenian soil.
- The new Slovenian government is unlikely to be composed before the end of December, analysts said.
- More than 340 exhibitors from 17 countries participate in the seventh furniture fair that started in Ljubljana on Tuesday.

- If current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek does not hold on to his post, then he would seriously consider candidacy as Secretary General of the United nations Organisation, a source close to the government said on Tuesday. REUTER
